subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 3: Grammar – Present perfect with since and for
outcomes: Know when to use since and when to use for.
Ask and answer How long questions with the Present perfect.
Talk about yourself using since and for.

tf.s: We use since with a point in time, like 2016.
We use for with a period of time, like five years.
tf.why: Yes: for five years, for a long time.

tf.s: “I've had my watch since two years” is correct.
tf.why: Two years is a period, so we say for two years.

tf.s: “He has been a puppeteer since he was eight” is correct.
tf.why: He was eight is a point in time.

tf.s: We say “How long has she lived in Sur?”
tf.why: She takes has in the Present perfect.

tf.s: “I haven't been to the cinema for I was seven” is correct.
tf.why: I was seven is a point in time, so use since.
2019 is a point in time: since 2019.

tf.s: The Present perfect is have/has + past participle.
tf.why: For example: I have known, she has lived.

tf.s: We say “How long have you had your bike?”
Majid's uncle has been a comedian since ten years.
tf.why: Ten years is a period: for ten years.

boxes.why: Five years is a period of time.

boxes.q: My uncle has worked at the aquarium ___ 2016.
How long ___ she lived in Sur?
Frank has had his costume ___ a long time.
boxes.why: A long time is a period.

boxes.q: Which time words go with since?
boxes.why: Points in time go with since.

boxes.q: Which time words go with for?
boxes.why: Periods of time go with for.

boxes.q: Sara has ___ her phone for two years.
boxes.why: Present perfect uses the past participle: had.

boxes.q: We use How long + Present perfect to ask about ___.
boxes.why: It asks how much time from the past until now.

mcq.why: Since + a point in time, e.g. since 2016.
For + a period, e.g. for five years.

mcq.q: Complete: Majid's uncle has been a comedian ___ ten years.
mcq.why: Ten years is a period of time.

mcq.q: since or for? He has been a puppeteer ___ he was eight.
mcq.why: He was eight is a point in time.

mcq.q: Make a question: you / have / your bike / how long?
o: How long have you had your bike?
How long you have had your bike?
How long has you had your bike?
How long did you have your bike now?
mcq.why: How long + have + subject + past participle.

mcq.q: Change to a question: He has played football for five years.
o: How long has he played football?
How long have he played football?
How long he has played football?
How long is he play football?
mcq.why: He takes has; the subject comes after has.

mcq.q: Correct the mistake: I haven't been to the cinema for I was seven.
o: I haven't been to the cinema since I was seven.
I haven't been to the cinema for I am seven.
I haven't went to the cinema for I was seven.
I hasn't been to the cinema since I was seven.
mcq.why: I was seven is a point in time, so use since.

o: I've had my watch for two years.
I've had my watch since two years.
I have my watch since two years.
mcq.why: Two years is a period, so use for.

mcq.q: Ahmed got his bike on his birthday and still has it. Which sentence is right?
o: Ahmed has had his bike since his birthday.
Ahmed has had his bike for his birthday.
Ahmed had his bike since his birthday.
Ahmed has his bike for his birthday.
mcq.why: His birthday is a point in time and he still has it.

mcq.q: Huda moved to Muscat eight years ago and still lives there. Which is correct?
o: Huda has lived in Muscat for eight years.
Huda has lived in Muscat since eight years.
Huda lived in Muscat for eight years ago.
Huda is living in Muscat since eight years.
mcq.why: Eight years is a period of time, so use for.
